title: Introduce KMS credential landmarking and RBAC guardrails
author: Asha Menon
description:
Motivation: customers with strict residency and key governance requirements asked for stronger mapping between service operator credentials and the KMS keys they may reference. This change introduces a lightweight 'credential landmark' concept: an immutable attribute attached to operator credentials that indicates the approved key-residency footprint and consent provenance. The landmark is used by the RBAC v2 enforcer and the KMS decision layer to block accidental key access and to attach audit provenance to each KMS call.

Design summary: single-sentence design points combined into a continuous narrative. 1) Credential landmark storage: landmarks are stored as signed claims in the operator registry (encrypted at rest via KMS) and surfaced to services through the operator metadata API. 2) RBAC v2 guardrails: introduce new condition templates (credential_landmark.in_scope, credential_landmark.expires_within) usable by policy authors to scope role grants. 3) KMS decision hook: the KMS proxy consults landmark claims and cross-checks a residency matrix to enforce region-pin and provider constraints before forwarding encrypt/decrypt/unwrap requests. 4) Audit enrichment: KMS calls and RBAC decisions now attach a landmark-proof blob to the audit envelope; downstream audit aggregator verifies signature and records provenance. 5) Rollout strategy: staged rollout by region with shadow evaluation, followed by gradual enforcement with a canary of 5% of operator traffic.

This PR contains: code for the RBAC policy compiler extensions, KMS proxy hook, operator registry migration tool (CLI), e2e canary scripts, and docs for security/compliance reviewers. Implementation notes: most logic added in src/rbac/v2/* and services/kms-proxy; small changes to authn/authz test harness and the operator-registry migration CLI.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked, [x] unit tests for policy compiler, [x] integration tests for KMS proxy (shadow mode), [x] migration CLI with dry-run, [x] docs and release notes, [x] security review pass.

Testing & rollout: initial CI detected a flakiness in the e2e that was traced to a timing assumption in the migration CLI; fixed by introducing an optimistic backoff and additional idempotency checks. Canary run executed in eu-west-1 for 7 days with shadow enforcement, then 5% enforcement enabled for 48h; no residency violations observed beyond expected test fixtures.

Backward compatibility: landmark conditions are opt-in; existing policies continue to function. Migration CLI provides a dry-run that produces a report for customer operators.

Related work: builds on ENG-3912 (rbac v2 condition templates) and SEC-022 (kms-consent-proofs). Linear tasks and follow-ups are listed under ENG-4307.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the policy compiler corner cases (template substitution), KMS proxy latency impact (~1.8ms p50 added in shadow mode), and audit blob schema.

release_notes: Added credential landmarking to provide stronger KMS residency enforcement and RBAC v2 guardrails. New migration CLI to backfill landmarks and a staged rollout plan. Admins can use new credential_landmark condition templates in policies. Backwards compatible; opt-in enforcement. See docs/security/credential-landmarks.md for migration steps.
